final_rationale: The verdict changes because the Actor narrowed an overbroad certification claim to a policy-bounded one; no genuinely new admissible evidence was added. On the original framing, the claim was suspicious because aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general external governance guidance did not satisfy the internal predicate for certification without material caveats, especially given the draft-only mitigation record. In the response, the Actor expressly concedes those limits and no longer treats the draft mitigation as approved closure. That narrower position is materially different: it aligns with the available policy text by allowing, at most, certification on a disclosed-limitation basis rather than clean certification. This is enough for compliant_with_caveats, not clean compliance, because the unresolved limitation, missing approved mitigation fields, and absence of identified approved risk acceptance remain live compliance conditions.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided; evidence access remains actor-summary-only, so the exact scope and wording of the internal artifacts cannot be independently verified.

The record still does not identify an approved risk-acceptance document for the utility arrears assistance limitation.

Caveated compliance is supportable only if the certification packet explicitly discloses the unresolved limitation for the named launch use case and does not imply that draft monitoring artifacts constitute approved closure.
